It questioned what its 25.1 per cent holding offered beyond a board seat and a share of the losses, while saying the strategic logic of the investment still held. In a letter to the newspaper responding to that commentary, Juliet Teo, joint head of portfolio development at Temasek Singapore, said Temasek viewed SIA's decision to invest in Air India from a long-term perspective and was supportive of it. The letter said the transformation of Air India involved complex, multi-year operational and integration challenges, with outcomes shaped by industry developments and external factors such as airspace disruptions, geopolitical developments and fuel price volatility. "Efforts of this scale take time and are not expected to be linear," it said. Temasek did not address whether it would support any capital contribution by SIA to Air India. Air India's multibillion-dollar revamp has been under way since Tata took control of the former state-owned carrier in 2022. Air India has been hit by Pakistan's airspace ban on Indian carriers, disruptions from the US-Israeli war with Iran and the fallout from a crash last year that killed 260 people. In the year to March, the airline and its budget unit Air India Express posted combined losses of US$2.33 billion, weighing on SIA's profits. SIA said on Thursday its board would carefully consider any requests for additional capital from Air India, taking into consideration the group's other capital requirements and Air India's business strategy.

item.title: Astros to toss patchwork of pitchers against Mets
item.description: The Houston Astros will have to cobble together their pitching plans for the final two games of their weekend series against the New York Mets.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Houston Astros will have to cobble together their pitching plans for the final two games of their weekend series against the New York Mets. Thanks to Hunter Brown and an assist from the Milwaukee Brewers, such a piecemeal problem is a lot less concerning than it might have been entering Friday. The Astros will look to continue their resurgence Saturday afternoon when they visit the Mets in the second contest of the three-game interleague set. Left-hander Bennett Sousa (1-3, 6.27 ERA) will serve as an opener for the Astros in his first big league start. Cristian Javier (1-4, 6.47 ERA) likely will follow in a bulk relief role. Right-hander Nolan McLean (9-8, 3.21) is slated to start for the Mets. Brown struck out a season-high 10 batters over 6 2/3 innings Friday night, when he earned the win as the Astros beat the Mets, 3-1. Brown's gem, coupled with the Milwaukee Brewers' 6-1 win over the Texas Rangers, increased Houston's American League West lead over the second-place Rangers to two games. The Astros will win any tiebreaker by virtue of a 9-4 edge in the season series with their Lone Star State rivals. The Astros are 3-1 since the exit of general manager Dana Brown on Monday. Houston, which is trying to return to the playoffs after its streak of nine straight postseason appearances was snapped last year, continued tinkering Thursday, when former pitching coach Brent Strom returned to the team as a consultant. Strom, pitching coach Joshua Miller and assistant pitching coach Ethan Katz will be tasked with figuring out a way to repair a rotation that has issued a league-high 330 walks while compiling a 5.11 ERA - third-worst in the majors - and averaging just 4.9 innings per outing. Neither Javier nor whomever starts Sunday's game - the Astros currently have "TBD" as their probable pitcher - likely are to approach the length provided Friday by Brown, who was the first Astros pitcher to pitch at least six innings since Hayden Wesneski lasted seven innings against the San Francisco Giants on Aug. 10. "That's huge, just to get him out there in the seventh and us being able to save some bullets for the next few days," Astros manager Joe Espada said. McLean has provided plenty of relief for the Mets' bullpen by lasting at least six innings in 12 of his last 14 starts. He's gone 6-4 with a 2.40 ERA in that span to drop his overall ERA from 4.21 to 3.21 - the lowest it has been since McLean had a 2.92 ERA following his start on May 14. McLean has gone at least six innings 17 times overall in 26 starts this season - more than twice as often as Sean Manaea, who ranks second on the Mets with eight outings of six innings or more. "I wouldn't say I am any stronger or any better than I felt to start the season," McLean said following his start against the Chicago White Sox last Sunday, when he tossed six scoreless innings of one-hit ball and didn't factor into the decision in the Mets' 2-1 loss. "It's just every time I go out there, I am trying to learn and hopefully doing a better job of that." Sousa took the defeat in his most recent outing Wednesday night, when he gave up four runs while recording just one out in the Astros' 9-3 loss to the Yankees. Javier last pitched Sunday, when he didn't factor into the decision after allowing three runs over four innings as the starter in a 7-6 loss to the Athletics. Sousa has never opposed the Mets. Javier didn't factor into the decision in his lone start against New York on June 21, 2023, when he surrendered four runs over 2 1/3 innings in the Astros' 10-8 victory. McLean has never faced the Astros. -Field Level Media

item.title: Braves seek sixth straight win, as they face woeful Rockies
item.description: The Atlanta Braves will continue their quest to avoid the wild-card round in October when they host the Colorado Rockies in the second game of their three-game series on Saturday night.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: The Atlanta Braves will continue their quest to avoid the wild-card round in October when they host the Colorado Rockies in the second game of their three-game series on Saturday night. The National League-East leaders defeated the Rockies 6-4 on Friday and enter the Saturday contest a game behind the Los Angeles Dodgers in the chase for the No. 2 seed in the league. The top two seeds earn byes straight into the NL Division Series. Atlanta helped its cause by sweeping the Dodgers in a trio of one-run games ahead of the series against the Rockies and extended its winning streak to five games with Friday's triumph. The Braves can make it two in a row against the Rockies when they send left-hander Martin Perez (8-8, 3.12 ERA) to the mound. Colorado will counter with right-hander Ryan Feltner (5-8, 6.08) Perez is slated to make his ninth career start against Colorado and is 2-3 with a 3.60 ERA in his eight previous outings. He is following two strong starts by Chris Sale and Grant Holmes in wins over the Dodgers and Rockies, respectively. It also comes after the team announced two of its starters, Spencer Schwellenbach and Hurston Waldrep, are done for the season and will undergo elbow surgery. The Braves have been winning despite Ronald Acuna Jr.'s struggles in August. A career .284 hitter, he is batting .235 on the season and .227 in August. Manager Walt Weiss gave him Thursday off. Acuna responded with three hits and a walk, and he also made a sliding catch in right field. "I've talked about this, picking spots for guys when I think I feel like maybe they can use some help slowing things down," Weiss said Thursday. "We talk about the fact that I think with everyday players, the best way to slow the game down, or one of the best ways, is to have them watch it in the dugout." Colorado's Hunter Goodman returned Tuesday from a left shoulder strain that cost him 10 games. He made an impact right away, homering in each of his first two games back against the host Nationals to give him a career-high 36 homers. He added three hits Friday night. The two-time All-Star catcher continues to impress manager Warren Schaeffer. "He's awesome," Schaeffer said. "He's our All-Star. He's got 30-plus homers. It's always great to get a guy like that back in the lineup. He feels good, which is even better." Even with Goodman's strong season, the Rockies are on pace to lose 100 games again, although they already surpassed last season's 43 wins with more than a month remaining in the season. Still, at 52-83, Colorado has the worst record in the NL. One of the disappointments is Feltner's recent outings. He had a serviceable June, posting a 4.00 ERA in five starts, but followed that with a 9.68 ERA in July and a 7.00 ERA in four August starts. He is 3-6 in the nine starts. His past two starts have been especially tough. He allowed seven runs in a 7-6 loss to the Dodgers on Aug. 18, then gave up seven runs (five earned) to the Nationals on Monday. He is facing Atlanta for the fifth time in his career, and is 0-4 with an 11.25 ERA in his previous four starts. He has given up six home runs in 16 innings. --Field Level Media

item.title: Cardinals follow innings limit as Kyle Leahy faces Pirates
item.description: Right-hander Kyle Leahy has been a bright spot for the St. Louis Cardinals this season, but to protect his promising future, the team is limiting his innings the rest of the way.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Right-hander Kyle Leahy has been a bright spot for the St. Louis Cardinals this season, but to protect his promising future, the team is limiting his innings the rest of the way. Leahy (10-4, 3.13 ERA) makes his 26th start Saturday afternoon, facing the visiting Pittsburgh Pirates in the second contest of a three-game set. The Cards opened the series with a 4-1 victory Friday night. A big key was the performance of rookie left-hander Quinn Mathews, who allowed a run and struck out seven over 5 2/3 innings for his first major league win. With Mathews pitching into the sixth, and right-hander Ryan Fernandez following with two scoreless innings, the rest of the pitching staff got a much-needed break. And it was important with Leahy starting the next game. "That's exactly what's needed," Cardinals manager Oliver Marmol said. "Knowing that you have a shorter start with our guy Leahy tomorrow, Quinn being able to do what he did today was very important." Leahy's 126 1/3 innings are his most since posting 144 2/3 in 2022 between Double-A Springfield and Triple-A Memphis. Leahy, 29, had been a reliever for the Cardinals in his first two full major league seasons. Leahy pitched at least six innings on six occasions this season, including three straight starts in July. He's been scaling back in August and threw just four scoreless, two-hit innings in his previous start Sunday in a 6-4 loss to the Philadelphia Phillies. The Cardinals are 4 1/2 games behind the final spot in the NL wild-card race, trailing the San Diego Padres, Arizona Diamondbacks, and Miami Marlins. But having Leahy healthy going into next season weighs heavily, even with the Cardinals still on the fringe of postseason contention in 2026. Against the Pirates, he's posted a 1.93 ERA with 22 strikeouts in 14 innings the past two seasons combined. He got the win in an 11-7 victory in a start that lasted 5 1/3 innings at Pittsburgh on April 28. Pirates slugger Oneil Cruz homered that day. The Pirates have faded from postseason contention and now just want to return to the higher-quality play they showed during the first few months of the season. They've had trouble scoring runs on their current road trip, and they made three errors in the field against the Cardinals in the series opener. Pirates manager Don Kelly said his team wants to reset after an inconsistent stretch on both sides of the ball. "We need to get back to doing what we do, which we've talked a lot about -- keeping the line moving, finding a way to have team at-bats, and trusting each other going through the process," Kelly said. "We're getting outside of that right now. Guys going up there trying to carry it, and it's not on any one player personally." Lake Bachar (1-3, 3.70) will start as an opener for the Pirates, with fellow right-hander Carmen Mlodzinski (6-6, 4.17) expected to follow as a bulk reliever. In 11 career appearances (four starts) Mlodzinski is 3-0 with a 1.75 ERA. --Field Level Media

item.title: Kremlin dice que considera a UE una entidad hostil, sin perspectivas de que mejoren las relaciones
item.description: Europa está haciendo declaraciones que sugieren que considera a Rusia como un "adversario e, incluso, un enemigo", afirmó el sábado el portavoz del Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, quien añadió que Moscú no ve perspectivas de mejora en las relaciones entre Rusia y la Unión Europea.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Europa está haciendo declaraciones que sugieren que considera a Rusia como un "adversario e, incluso, un enemigo", afirmó el sábado el portavoz del Kremlin, Dmitri Peskov, quien añadió que Moscú no ve perspectivas de mejora en las relaciones entre Rusia y la Unión Europea. No quedó claro de inmediato a qué declaraciones se refería Peskov. Añadió que los actuales dirigentes políticos de la UE mantienen una actitud conflictiva hacia Rusia, "no solo de palabra, sino también de hecho". "Están movilizando las capacidades militares de Europa y dirigiéndolas contra nuestro país, al tiempo que participan directamente en las hostilidades contra nosotros", afirmó.

item.title: Le Népal reprend ses opérations de sauvetage, sollicite une aide et des milliards de dollars
item.description: Le Népal a repris samedi les opérations de recherche et de sauvetage après une brève interruption due aux conditions météorologiques alors que près de 3.000 personnes sont toujours portées disparues à la suite d'une inondation dévastatrice qui a fait des centaines de morts et ravagé une région limitrophe du Tibet.
item.dc:creator: Gopal Sharma, Saurabh Sharma, Sahana Bajracharya, Liz Lee
item.content:encoded: Le Népal a repris samedi les opérations de recherche et de sauvetage après une brève interruption due aux conditions météorologiques alors que près de 3.000 personnes sont toujours portées disparues à la suite d'une inondation dévastatrice qui a fait des centaines de morts et ravagé une région limitrophe du Tibet. Le Népal , qui compte 30 millions d'habitants, a sollicité l'aide de spécialistes étrangers et son ministre des Finances a déclaré à Reuters qu'il aurait également besoin d'environ 4 à 5 milliards de dollars pour se reconstruire après la catastrophe. Provoquée par l'effondrement d'un glacier, une coulée de roches, de glace, de boue et de débris s'est déchaînée mercredi dans les cours d'eau de montagne, tuant au moins 669 personnes au Népal et sept au Tibet chinois, et emportant sur son passage des bâtiments, des ponts et des centrales électriques. Près de 3.000 personnes sont toujours portées disparues, dont environ 2.426 au Népal et 554 dans le comté de Gyirong au Tibet, parmi lesquelles au moins 540 ressortissants étrangers, pour la plupart des pèlerins hindous venus d'Inde. DES CORPS DÉCOMPOSÉS ET MÉCONNAISSABLES Les opérations de recherche et de sauvetage ont été temporairement suspendues en raison de la pluie et du brouillard, mais elles ont repris dans le courant de l'après-midi, a déclaré un officier de police du district de Rasuwa, l’un des plus touchés. "Les hélicoptères survolent la zone et l'opération a repris suite à une légère amélioration des conditions météorologiques”, a-t-il déclaré, sous couvert d'anonymat. Les autorités avaient également suspendu les opérations de sauvetage vendredi lorsqu'un lac, formé à la frontière entre le Népal et la Chine à la suite des inondations, avait commencé à déborder dans les rivières népalaises Lhende Khola et Trishuli. Samedi, le risque s'était atténué et certaines parties du lit du lac étaient visibles, ont indiqué les autorités chinoises et la chaîne publique CCTV. Des images satellites suggéraient que l'eau s'écoulait lentement du lac, réduisant progressivement sa taille, a rapporté CCTV. Ce lac est l'un des deux situés en amont de la zone inondée et surveillés par le Népal. Les risques d'inondation persisteront jusqu'à ce que les deux se soient entièrement vidés, a averti un responsable. Trois jours après la catastrophe, les autorités ont indiqué que certains corps repêchés étaient dans un état de décomposition tel qu'ils étaient méconnaissables. Ils seront inhumés après l'accomplissement des formalités légales en raison des risques sanitaires et de la crainte d'épidémies. "Des échantillons d'ADN seront prélevés, puis les corps seront enterrés dans un espace ouvert", a indiqué l'administration du district de Chitwan dans un communiqué. LES FAMILLES À LA RECHERCHE DES DISPARUS À Katmandou, les familles des personnes disparues se sont rassemblées devant le campus médical de Maharajgunj, où certains corps avaient été transportés. Beaucoup ont tenté d'identifier des proches à partir des photos des corps affichées sur les portails et les murs d'enceinte. En Malaisie, les familles de 91 citoyens répertoriés comme "injoignables" au Tibet et au Népal attendaient également des nouvelles. Manivannan Rethinam, représentant de certains d'entre eux, a exhorté le ministère des Affaires étrangères à mettre en place un canal de communication permettant d'obtenir des informations plus rapidement, affirmant que le manque d'informations était "profondément douloureux" pour les proches en attente de nouvelles. Le ministère indien des Affaires extérieures a déclaré que 275 ressortissants indiens manquaient à l'appel. Le ministère des Affaires étrangères de la Malaisie a indiqué de son côté que les opérations de recherche, de sauvetage et de vérification se poursuivaient. Pour les survivants, l'épreuve est loin d'être terminée, car ils doivent désormais reconstruire leur vie. Saraswati Ghale, âgée 43 ans, a raconté que sa maison avait été détruite par les inondations. Elle se souvient s'être précipitée vers les hauteurs lorsque l'eau a déferlé, faisant trembler le sol "comme s'il y avait un tremblement de terre". "Je n'ai plus rien (…) Je suis sauvée, mais qui sait comment les choses vont évoluer", a-t-elle déclaré.

item.title: Liverpool cierra acuerdo con PSG por Barcola: medios
item.description: El Liverpool cerró un acuerdo para fichar al delantero francés Bradley Barcola, de 23 años, procedente del París Saint-Germain, en una operación por 123 millones de libras esterlinas (166,43 millones de dólares), según informaron los medios el sábado, con lo que se convertirá en el último fichaje estrella de la plantilla de Andoni Iraola.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Liverpool cerró un acuerdo para fichar al delantero francés Bradley Barcola, de 23 años, procedente del París Saint-Germain, en una operación por 123 millones de libras esterlinas (166,43 millones de dólares), según informaron los medios el sábado, con lo que se convertirá en el último fichaje estrella de la plantilla de Andoni Iraola. El club inglés, 20 veces campeón de la Premier League, pagará por Barcola un importe total de 106 millones de libras, con complementos que podrían elevar la cifra en 17 millones de libras, según la BBC. The Athletic informó de que el jugador firmará un contrato de cinco años. Reuters se puso en contacto con el Liverpool y el PSG para recabar sus comentarios. Barcola se incorporó al PSG procedente del Olympique de Lyon, el club de su infancia, en 2023, y disfrutó de una etapa repleta de trofeos en la capital francesa, con dos títulos consecutivos de la Liga de Campeones en las temporadas 2024-25 y 2025-26, tres títulos de la Ligue 1 y dos Copas de Francia, entre otros galardones. Disputó 152 partidos en todas las competiciones con el PSG, en los que marcó 39 goles y dio 37 asistencias. Le quedaban dos años de contrato con el PSG. Barcola sería el último fichaje de la plantilla del nuevo entrenador, Andoni Iraola, tras las incorporaciones durante el mercado de verano del defensa uruguayo Ronald Araujo, cedido, el central francés Jeremy Jacquet y el delantero español Víctor Muñoz. Las opciones ofensivas del Liverpool incluyen actualmente al fichaje más caro de la historia del fútbol británico, Alexander Isak, además de Cody Gakpo, Rio Ngumoha y Muñoz, mientras el club de Merseyside se adapta a la vida tras la marcha de su figura emblemática, Mohamed Salah. El delantero Hugo Ekitike también se encuentra de baja por una lesión de larga duración. (1 dólar = 0,7390 libras)

item.title: Russia extends ban on diesel exports until September 30
item.description: Russia said on Saturday it had extended a ban on diesel exports until September 30.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Russia said on Saturday it had extended a ban on diesel exports until September 30. The ban also covers exports of marine fuel and gas oils shipped by Russian producers, the government said in a statement. "These measures have been taken to stabilise the domestic fuel market," it said. Three sources previously [USN:L6N44M0KS TEXT:"told"] Reuters that Russia would extend the ban as domestic fuel shortages persist, with several refineries still offline after repeated Ukrainian [USN:L6N4480EU TEXT:"drone attacks"]. Russia [USN:L6N43A0YA TEXT:"introduced"] the export ban from July 8 to July 31 as part of a broader package of measures to support the domestic fuel market, before [USN:L8N43V0XS TEXT:"extending"] it for fuel producers until August 31. Russia has also banned exports of diesel by non-producers and motor gasoline until January 31, 2027, and jet fuel until the end of November 2026. Russia is typically the world's second-largest diesel exporter after the U.S. Exports had already slowed before the ban because of domestic shortages linked to Ukrainian drone attacks.

item.title: Giants to retire Jeff Kent's number between games of twin bill with D-backs
item.description: Two teams with uncertainty at second base will get an opportunity to watch a Hall of Fame second baseman get his number retired when the San Francisco Giants honor Jeff Kent in between games of a day-night doubleheader Saturday against the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks.
item.dc:creator: Field Level Media
item.content:encoded: Two teams with uncertainty at second base will get an opportunity to watch a Hall of Fame second baseman get his number retired when the San Francisco Giants honor Jeff Kent in between games of a day-night doubleheader Saturday against the visiting Arizona Diamondbacks. The rare twin bill was created when the Giants were forced to schedule a rainout-makeup game Monday in Atlanta, prompting Sunday's series finale against the Diamondbacks to be converted into a Saturday doubleheader. Kent's ceremony was originally scheduled to be held before the single game on Saturday. Instead, it will lead into the nightcap. As they went their separate ways following a 3-hour, 6-minute marathon on Friday night, won 10-6 by the Diamondbacks, only one of Saturday's four starting pitchers had been announced. Arizona has scheduled right-hander Merrill Kelly (8-12, 5.35 ERA), who is 10-5 with a 3.26 ERA in 23 lifetime starts against the Giants, for the first game. The Diamondbacks will start Mitch Bratt (1-2, 4.54) in the second game of the doubleheader. Bratt has never faced the Giants. He took a no-decision last Sunday in a 5-3 win over Cincinnati, allowing five hits and three runs in three innings, walking three and striking out three. Interestingly, the 37-year-old Kelly was drafted by the Baltimore Orioles (but did not sign) while in high school in 2007, one year before Kent retired as a member of the Los Angeles Dodgers. Kent had played 900 games over six seasons for the Giants, hitting 175 of his 377 home runs in orange and black and earning the retirement of his No. 21 jersey. Kelly didn't make his major league debut until 2019 and never faced Kent. Only one player likely to be active for Saturday's doubleheader -- 35-year-old Diamondbacks infielder Ildemaro Vargas -- was in professional baseball, playing in the Venezuelan Summer League -- the year Kent retired. Vargas has taken over at second base for the Diamondbacks since two-time All-Star Ketel Marte left the team last week and landed on the injured list, dealing with left knee inflammation. Marte is eligible to be reinstated Monday. Vargas had a two-run single in Friday's win, making him 6-for-43 (.140) with five RBIs since becoming the starter at second base 11 games ago. Arizona manager Torey Lovullo insists Vargas, who has played all four infield positions, left field and has even pitched three times this season, means more to the club than his batting average might indicate. "Very engaged player. Plays with energy," the manager praised to reporters earlier this week. "He's looked at as somebody that is leading the charge emotionally." The Giants have had no such consistency as they've attempted to patch the hole left by the trade that sent their All-Star second baseman, Luis Arraez, to the Philadelphia Phillies last month. In their current homestand alone, Nate Furman (three), Shay Whitcomb (one) and Osleivis Basabe (one) have gotten starts at second, combining to go 2-for-16 with five strikeouts and a homer by Whitcomb on Wednesday against the Cincinnati Reds. Casey Schmitt, lost for the season following surgery to repair torn meniscus in his left knee, could be the long-term solution. "If there would be a positive spin to (Schmitt's injury), he's fresh and he's healed up for the start of the offseason, and he can kind of hit the ground running," Giants manager Tony Vitello noted to the media recently. "This was a breakout year for him, and I know everyone around him -- but nobody more than him -- wants to come back in a resounding way and make next year even better." Playing a variety of positions over 98 games this season, the 27-year-old hit a career-high 21 homers In 98 games. Kent hit just 20 homers in 125 games for the New York Mets as a 27-year-old in 1995, two seasons before joining the Giants. --Field Level Media

item.title: Haakon de Noruega homenajea a su "querido padre" Harald en primer discurso como soberano
item.description: El rey Haakon VIII de Noruega rindió homenaje a su difunto padre, al que calificó de "un padre tan bueno", en su primer discurso a la nación desde que asumió el trono, y su voz se quebró brevemente al evocar a su madre, la reina Sonja, ya viuda .
item.dc:creator: Nerijus Adomaitis, Janis Laizans, Dylan Martinez
item.content:encoded: El rey Haakon VIII de Noruega rindió homenaje a su difunto padre, al que calificó de "un padre tan bueno", en su primer discurso a la nación desde que asumió el trono, y su voz se quebró brevemente al evocar a su madre, la reina Sonja, ya viuda . El rey Harald, que salió de la sombra de su propio padre —muy querido y extrovertido— para convertirse en un reformista durante más de tres décadas en el trono, falleció el viernes a los 89 años. Haakon, vestido con traje negro, camisa blanca y corbata negra, elogió a Harald como un hombre de familia cariñoso en un discurso grabado y transmitido por televisión desde el palacio. "Mi querido padre, gracias por ser un padre tan bueno para Martha y para mí", dijo, refiriéndose a su hermana, la princesa Martha Louise. "Le voy a echar de menos. Voy a echar de menos su risa. Voy a echar de menos su forma afable de relacionarse con la gente y afrontar las situaciones", continuó, sentado tras un escritorio, con un retrato de un Harald sonriente a su izquierda. Señaló que ese sábado debería haber sido la celebración del 58º aniversario de boda de Harald y la reina Sonja, que le sobrevive. "Felicidades por su aniversario de boda, querida mamá", dijo Haakon, con la voz aparentemente embargada por la emoción durante un instante. UN PUEBLO Haakon subrayó que hará las cosas a su manera, como hizo su padre antes que él, y reiteró los fundamentos de Noruega como monarquía constitucional, encarnados en el juramento que prestará el martes en el Parlamento para proteger la Constitución y las leyes del país. "Creemos en nuestro sistema de autogobierno y en la democracia. Creemos en una sociedad basada en el Estado de derecho, en la que todas las personas tienen el mismo valor", afirmó. Haakon se convirtió de forma automática en rey tras la muerte de su padre, de acuerdo con la monarquía constitucional de Noruega. No habrá coronación, ya que estas fueron abolidas por el Parlamento en 1908. "Creemos en una Noruega en la que haya sitio para todos. Sentiremos la fuerza de nuestra comunidad y sabremos, en lo más profundo de nuestro ser, que somos un solo pueblo", señaló. Al final de su discurso, frente al palacio, las personas que habían estado siguiendo el acto en sus teléfonos móviles estallaron en un aplauso espontáneo. En declaraciones a Reuters minutos antes del discurso, el primer ministro, Jonas Gahr Stoere, señaló que Haakon comparte muchas cualidades con su padre. "Este rey ha heredado algo de su padre, y es la capacidad de crear un ambiente de unión", comentó en una entrevista frente al palacio. TOLERANCIA E INCLUSIÓN Desde el fallecimiento de Harald, decenas de miles de personas han acudido en masa para despedirse del difunto rey en el palacio real, donde yace su capilla ardiente, y muchos de los asistentes recordaron su espíritu de inclusión y tolerancia. Las banderas ondearon a media asta en todo el país y se pudieron ver los retratos del difunto rey con uniforme de gala en paradas de autobús, tranvías y estaciones de metro, así como en tiendas, oficinas y edificios públicos. La avenida principal del centro de Oslo, Karl Johan, estaba abarrotada de gente de todos los ámbitos de la vida que se dirigía hacia el palacio, con flores, tarjetas escritas a mano, dibujos y pequeñas banderas nacionales en las manos. Los dolientes elogiaron el espíritu de inclusión del difunto rey. "Significó mucho para nosotros, los inmigrantes (…) Nos sentimos realmente muy incluidos. Por eso, gracias a él, me siento tan noruega", declaró a Reuters Veselina Vitanova, una profesora de 43 años originaria de Bulgaria, a las puertas del palacio. Otra persona se refirió a un discurso que Harald pronunció en 2016 y que se hizo viral en todo el mundo, en el que dijo: "Los noruegos son chicas que aman a chicas, chicos que aman a chicos y chicas y chicos que se aman entre sí". "Eso resume cómo se sentía él respecto a las personas y cómo quería que los noruegos nos sintiéramos los unos con los otros", afirmó Mari Eidsvaag, de 32 años, que llevaba una camiseta con esa frase, un arcoíris y un dibujo del rey Harald. "Creo que es una declaración muy importante, sobre todo en estos tiempos", declaró a Reuters.

item.title: Marquez brothers go one-two at Aragon as Marc claims record 20th sprint win
item.description: Marc Marquez beat his younger brother Alex to win the Aragon Grand Prix sprint on Saturday, as the reigning MotoGP champion underlined his dominance on home turf and at one of his favourite tracks.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Marc Marquez beat his younger brother Alex to win the Aragon Grand Prix sprint on Saturday, as the reigning MotoGP champion underlined his dominance on home turf and at one of his favourite tracks. Victory also gave Marc a hat-trick of sprint wins at Aragon as the seven-times MotoGP champion moved up to third in the championship standings with 212 points, behind leader Jorge Martin (245) and Marco Bezzecchi (216). Bezzecchi had claimed [USN:L4N44Q01W TEXT:"pole position with a lap record"] earlier on Saturday, but he had a poor start off the line, with both Marc and Alex overtaking the Aprilia rider to drop him down to third after turn one in the 11-lap sprint. Once Marc was out in front, there was no catching him as he peeled away with Alex in tow, while Bezzecchi found no opening to attack the two Ducati bikes, which both had medium compound rear tyres compared with the Italian's soft rear tyre. "I knew that Marco was with the soft tyres so the (best) chance of (winning) the race was at the first corner," Marc said after a record 20th sprint win in MotoGP. "Tomorrow will be a bit of the same, so let's see. Of course, a good start helped a lot and I was riding at a good pace but I saw that the group was also quite fast, especially Alex. "Let's see if tomorrow we can improve a bit (in the race) and try to be as consistent as today." HOME CROWD The Marquez one-two mirrored last year's Aragon sprint, delighting the home crowd as fans, who had packed into stands bearing the brothers' names, roared as they collected their medals. Marc, a seven-times race winner at Aragon, dived down the inside of turn one to take the lead, nudging Bezzecchi aside and creating a gap that Alex also capitalised on to slip past the Italian. "I knew Marc and Alex had something more. Unfortunately, I missed a little bit the braking point in the first corner," Bezzecchi said. Behind them, Bezzecchi's teammate Martin lost position while fighting with Trackhouse Racing's Raul Fernandez and KTM's Pedro Acosta. However, Martin eventually managed to find his way past Fernandez. Although Martin finished fifth behind Acosta, he collected enough points to ensure he would retain his championship lead regardless of Sunday's race result.

item.title: Munoz earns Liverpool draw with Forest, Hull up to second, Newcastle beat Spurs
item.description: Liverpool's Victor Munoz struck a late equaliser to salvage a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, but Andoni Iraola's side were left still searching for their first Premier League win this season after his first home league game.
item.dc:creator: Lori Ewing
item.content:encoded: Liverpool's Victor Munoz struck a late equaliser to salvage a 2-2 draw against Nottingham Forest on Saturday, but Andoni Iraola's side were left still searching for their first Premier League win this season after his first home league game. Forest had looked set to leave Anfield with all three points, in what would have been a first league victory in charge for Oliver Glasner, when Morgan Gibbs-White converted a 70th-minute penalty, awarded after Liverpool goalkeeper Alisson fouled Neco Williams in the area, for a 2-1 lead. But newcomer Munoz, in his first start for Liverpool, equalised in the 82nd minute, when he spun and blasted a shot from the edge of the box that went in off the crossbar. Newcastle United piled the pressure on Tottenham Hotspur coach Roberto De Zerbi with a 2-0 win in Saturday's late game, with second-half goals from Anthony Elanga and Yoane Wissa leaving Spurs with nothing to show for an improved performance. Spurs spurned several first-half chances before Elanga scored his second goal in as many league games and Wissa's acrobatic finish 10 minutes later ended the contest to deepen the gloom around the Tottenham Hotspur Stadium. Elsewhere, Bournemouth were held to a 1-1 draw by Everton, while Hull City left it late to beat fellow promoted side Coventry City 1-0 to move provisionally up to second place. FOREST LED AT HALF-TIME Forest had opened the scoring at Anfield through Dan Ndoye in the 24th minute, the Swiss forward finishing off a rapid counterattack that began with goalkeeper Matz Sels launching a long ball upfield before Gibbs-White slipped him through to slot coolly into the bottom corner. Liverpool had a first-half effort from Florian Wirtz chalked off after a VAR review determined Jeremie Frimpong was offside in the build-up, before finally levelling in the 60th minute when Alexander Isak scored. Cody Gakpo twisted away from his marker on the right and whipped a low ball across the face of goal, with Isak tapping into an empty net. "It's been good. There is always time to get used to a new style," Isak said. "We are really working hard to try to play the game (Iraola) wants us to play, when we start doing that better I have no doubt the results will come as well." TWO DRAWS FOR LIVERPOOL, SPURS LOSE AGAIN Liverpool had needed a stoppage-time penalty from Dominik Szoboszlai to rescue a 2-2 draw with Newcastle in their league opener six days earlier. Iraola, appointed this summer after the club followed up its 2025 Premier League title with a disappointing fifth-place finish under Arne Slot last season, despite their £446 million spending spree a year ago, remains without a Liverpool win. Spurs, however, are still waiting for even a league goal this season despite a better showing than last weekend's bruising defeat at Brentford. New signing [USN:L4N44K026 TEXT:"Omar Marmoush"] showed glimpses on his debut and Mathys Tel impressed in a first half in which Spurs ought to have scored. Tel and Jan Paul van Hecke drew good saves from Lukas Hornicek, while Pedro Porro was denied by a superb block from Lewis Hall to keep things level at halftime. But Elanga struck in the 62nd minute, holding off Sandro Tonali – the former Newcastle midfielder whose every touch was booed by the away fans – before firing off the post and in. Wissa then put the game to bed with a tidy flick over his shoulder from close range, with Spurs going through the motions as the game petered out in an increasingly empty stadium. PROMOTED HULL SECOND Coventry and Hull had played two goalless draws in the second-tier Championship last season, but this time Hull took all three points after Liam Millar scored an 82nd-minute winner. The goal came against the run of play from a Coventry corner, which was cleared before Mohamed Belloumi released Millar from inside his own half and the Canadian had only the goalkeeper to beat to silence the home crowd. Hull, who beat Manchester United last week, have six points from two games and sit behind Manchester City on goal difference. On the south coast, Bournemouth's Alex Scott scored the opener for the home side just before halftime when he was set up by Evanilson, with the midfielder pulling the trigger from the edge of the box to beat Jordan Pickford in Everton's goal. However, Bournemouth were left to rue what could have been after they failed to clear a corner and Everton skipper James Tarkowski pounced in the 91st minute to earn the visitors a point.

item.title: Aseguradora alemana Allianz estudia la adquisición del gigante de asistencia en carretera AA: medio
item.description: La empresa de servicios financieros con sede en Alemania Allianz está barajando una oferta de adquisición de 5.000 millones de libras esterlinas (6.770 millones de dólares) por el grupo de asistencia en carretera AA, según informó Sky News el sábado.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: La empresa de servicios financieros con sede en Alemania Allianz está barajando una oferta de adquisición de 5.000 millones de libras esterlinas (6.770 millones de dólares) por el grupo de asistencia en carretera AA, según informó Sky News el sábado. AA, fundada por un grupo de aficionados al motor en 1905 y conocida en Reino Unido por sus vehículos de asistencia de color amarillo, fue sacada a bolsa por sus anteriores propietarios de capital riesgo en 2014 a 250 peniques por acción . Allianz (ALVG.DE) es una de las pocas partes que han mantenido conversaciones con los asesores de AA sobre un acuerdo, según Sky News, que añadió que la firma de capital riesgo EQT es otro de los postores. Los propietarios de capital riesgo de la AA han estado siguiendo un proceso denominado de doble vía durante la mayor parte de este año, en el que la alternativa a la venta era una salida a bolsa en la Bolsa de Londres, según Sky News. Ambas empresas se negaron a hacer comentarios. El Financial Times informó el año pasado de que la empresa británica de asistencia en carretera tenía previsto vender por 5.000 millones de libras y estaba buscando compradores. (1 dólar = 0,7390 libras)

item.title: Rusia dice que capturó tres pueblos en las regiones ucranianas de Donetsk y Sumy
item.description: El Ministerio de Defensa ruso afirmó el sábado que sus tropas habían capturado la localidad de Khrapivshchyna, en la región ucraniana de Sumy, así como Novoandriivka y Rubizhne, en la de Donetsk.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: El Ministerio de Defensa ruso afirmó el sábado que sus tropas habían capturado la localidad de Khrapivshchyna, en la región ucraniana de Sumy, así como Novoandriivka y Rubizhne, en la de Donetsk. El ministerio indicó a través de su canal de Telegram que había atacado un centro logístico en la región de Kiev donde se almacenaban componentes para misiles balísticos ucranianos. Reuters no pudo verificar de forma independiente la información.

Russian strike on Kyiv-area warehouse sparks detonation, killing 37

KYIV: At least 37 people were killed after a Russian drone strike on a Kyiv-area ammunition depot sparked a detonation, President Volodymyr Zelenskyy said on Saturday (Aug 29), vowing to punish suspected negligence in the second such incident in two months. The deadliest Russian strike in the Kyiv area this year came as Moscow's air attacks on the Ukrainian capital and surrounding region dragged into a third straight day, killing residents, damaging homes and derailing daily life. Dozens were also injured and hundreds evacuated from the area of the strike in the village of Myla, Zelenskyy said, where nearby infrastructure including residential buildings and a facility for the elderly and people with disabilities suffered "significant damage". The attack sparked widespread fires, officials said. Among those killed was the head of a neighbouring village who rushed to help.

"A terrible situation and terrible negligence on the part of those who stored explosives right next to people," Zelenskyy said in a video address.

Related:

Ukraine backers gather as war escalates, air defence runs low

CIA director warned Russia not to attack NATO members: US media

SECOND STRIKE-RELATED DETONATION IN TWO MONTHS The site of Friday's blast was a military facility that held artillery shells, mines and drones, among other ammunition, said the Ukrainian president. It followed a similar incident in the Kyiv-area town of Vyshneve last month, when 10 people were killed and hundreds of houses damaged after a strike triggered secondary explosions. "Another such crime - after what happened in Vyshneve - is absolutely unacceptable," Zelenskyy said. "I expect the details to be presented to the public promptly." He added that criminal cases had already been opened on charges of official negligence. Ukrainian officials rarely disclose damage to military targets from Russian attacks. In a statement on Saturday, Ukraine's Defence Ministry said all those responsible for weapons storage should complete a full audit of their locations.

Also read:

Ukraine says Russia fired North Korean missiles in deadly attack

DRONE SWARMS AIMED AT KYIV Nine other regions had been targeted in overnight strikes by Russia, Zelenskyy added, saying Kyiv in particular was under "virtually non-stop attack" from high-speed drones. Russia has escalated its air war on Ukraine with increasing numbers of elusive ballistic missiles and new high-speed drones, which Kyiv lacks the air defences to shoot down. On Saturday, sirens blared throughout the morning for a third straight day as Ukraine's air force warned of new waves of drones approaching the capital. The sound of air defences could be heard booming across the sky. Kyiv region governor Tymur Tkachenko said a 14-year-old girl was killed in a morning drone strike on the Boryspil district. In Kyiv, a 2-year-old girl was killed by a downed drone, Mayor Vitali Klitschko said on Saturday. Strikes in and around Kyiv on Thursday and Friday had damaged warehouses and homes, part of what some Ukrainian officials said was a campaign aimed at "paralysing" the city of several million.

Source: Reuters/rl

item.title: Soldados amotinados atacan el aeropuerto y la presidencia en la capital de Níger
item.description: Soldados amotinados en Níger atacaron a primera hora del sábado el aeropuerto y la presidencia en la capital, Niamey, provocando horas de intensos tiroteos y explosiones e interrumpiendo brevemente la emisión de la televisión y la radio estatales.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Soldados amotinados en Níger atacaron a primera hora del sábado el aeropuerto y la presidencia en la capital, Niamey, provocando horas de intensos tiroteos y explosiones e interrumpiendo brevemente la emisión de la televisión y la radio estatales. A última hora de la mañana, el Ministerio de Defensa afirmó que las fuerzas armadas estaban recuperando progresivamente el control de los lugares atacados durante la noche, pero fuentes de seguridad indicaron que los amotinados seguían presentes en el aeropuerto y que la situación general no está clara. El ataque supuso la última amenaza para el régimen de Abdourahamane Tiani, quien se hizo con el poder en un golpe de Estado en 2023. Tiani se había comprometido a mejorar la seguridad en este país del Sahel, uno de los principales productores de uranio, pero los ataques yihadistas han persistido. La televisión estatal, tras reanudar sus emisiones, emitió un mensaje en el que se afirmaba que soldados amotinados de una base en Niamey habían abierto fuego contra "lugares sensibles" de la ciudad. Las fuerzas de seguridad habían reaccionado con rapidez y "habían contenido estos disturbios", según la televisión estatal. A principios de este año, grupos afiliados a Al Qaeda y a Estado Islámico llevaron a cabo atentados tanto contra el aeropuerto civil como contra la base aérea militar, lo que contribuyó a la sospecha inicial de que los militantes podrían estar detrás del asalto a la capital. SOLDADOS SE SUMAN A LA REBELIÓN Un testigo de Reuters informó de disparos en el aeropuerto y fuertes explosiones en las primeras horas de la madrugada. A las 0900 GMT, el palacio presidencial parecía haber sido asegurado por tropas leales, pero la zona alrededor del aeropuerto seguía siendo objeto de disputas, según indicaron dos fuentes de seguridad y un diplomático. Dos fuentes indicaron que se habían enviado tropas leales para recuperar el control del aeropuerto, ya fuera mediante negociaciones o por la fuerza. En el asalto también participaron soldados de las localidades de Ouallam, Tera y Dosso, en el suroeste, según una fuente de seguridad de Níger e Yvan Guichaoua, investigador principal del Centro Internacional de Estudios sobre Conflictos de Bonn. Las tropas de esta zona han sufrido numerosas bajas en los combates contra la filial regional del Estado Islámico, y tanto analistas como fuentes de seguridad señalan que la frustración con el Gobierno va en aumento entre las unidades de primera línea. No estaba claro cuántos soldados aliados con los amotinados habían entrado en Niamey ni dónde se habían desplegado. MILITANTES ISLÁMICOS Y URANIO Níger, una nación de África Occidental rica en minerales con importantes recursos de uranio, petróleo y oro, ha estado gobernada por militares desde el golpe de Estado de julio de 2023 que derrocó al presidente Mohamed Bazoum. Al igual que sus vecinos Burkina Faso y Malí, no ha logrado cambiar el rumbo de su lucha contra las insurgencias islamistas vinculadas a Al Qaeda y a Estado Islámico, a pesar de las promesas de los gobernantes militares de mejorar la seguridad. La filial de Al Qaeda en África Occidental reivindicó la autoría de un atentado contra el aeropuerto de Niamey en junio, cinco meses después de que la "Provincia del Sahel" de Estado Islámico atacara el mismo lugar. Desde que tomó el poder, el Gobierno de Tiani se ha alejado de sus socios occidentales, ha estrechado los lazos con Rusia y ha roto con el bloque regional de la CEDEAO, uniéndose a Malí y Burkina Faso para formar el bloque disidente AES. Los disturbios se producen en un momento en que las autoridades endurecen el control sobre el sector del uranio, tras haber confiscado activos de la empresa francesa Orano. Níger fue un proveedor clave de combustible nuclear para Europa, representando cerca del 15% del suministro de uranio de Orano a plena capacidad. La semana pasada, el Gobierno reasignó las antiguas licencias de uranio de Orano y GoviEx a empresas respaldadas por el Estado, según un decreto.

item.title: China envía expertos a Nepal para colaborar en las labores de rescate en un túnel
item.description: China envió a Nepal a cinco expertos en túneles procedentes de la región del Tíbet para participar en las labores de rescate tras las inundaciones, según informó el sábado la agencia estatal de noticias china Xinhua.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: China envió a Nepal a cinco expertos en túneles procedentes de la región del Tíbet para participar en las labores de rescate tras las inundaciones, según informó el sábado la agencia estatal de noticias china Xinhua. La ayuda se envió en helicóptero, a petición del Gobierno de Nepal, para llevar a cabo operaciones de rescate en una central hidroeléctrica.

item.title: Rusia prorroga la prohibición de exportar gasóleo hasta el 30 de septiembre
item.description: Rusia anunció el sábado una prórroga a la prohibición de exportar gasóleo hasta el 30 de septiembre.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Rusia anunció el sábado una prórroga a la prohibición de exportar gasóleo hasta el 30 de septiembre. La prohibición también afecta a las exportaciones de combustible marítimo y gasóleos enviados por productores rusos, según indicó el Gobierno en un comunicado. "Estas medidas se han adoptado para estabilizar el mercado nacional de combustible", señaló. Tres fuentes habían informado previamente a Reuters de que Rusia prorrogaría la prohibición debido a que persiste la escasez de combustible en el mercado nacional, con varias refinerías aún fuera de servicio tras los repetidos ataques con drones ucranianos. Rusia introdujo la prohibición de exportación del 8 al 31 de julio como parte de un paquete más amplio de medidas para apoyar el mercado nacional de combustibles, antes de prorrogarla para los productores de combustible hasta el 31 de agosto. Rusia también ha prohibido las exportaciones de gasóleo por parte de entidades que no sean productoras, así como de gasolina de motor hasta el 31 de enero de 2027, y de combustible para aviones hasta finales de noviembre de 2026. Rusia suele ser el segundo mayor exportador mundial de gasóleo, después de Estados Unidos. Las exportaciones ya se habían ralentizado antes de la prohibición debido a la escasez interna provocada por los ataques con drones ucranianos.

item.title: India's HDFC Bank CEO Jagdishan to step down in October
item.description: India's largest private lender HDFC Bank said on Saturday that its Chief Executive Sashidhar Jagdishan has decided not to seek reappointment when his term ends at the end of October.
item.dc:creator: Ashwin Manikandan, Gopika Gopakumar
item.content:encoded: India's largest private lender HDFC Bank (HDBK.NS) said on Saturday that its Chief Executive Sashidhar Jagdishan has decided not to seek reappointment when his term ends at the end of October. Jagdishan had been expected to seek a third term, but the abrupt exit of a former chairman raised investor concerns about HDFC Bank, even though an external [USN:L4N42Y132 TEXT:"review"] concluded in June that there was no evidence to substantiate the governance issues the former chairman raised. In July, the bank's board penalised three top executives including Jagdishan after judging that employees involved in setting deposit rates for a state agency had engaged in [USN:L4N43T0QY TEXT:""business overreach""]. "Mr. Jagdishan reiterated his decision to not seek reappointment. Accordingly, he shall retire from the services of the Bank upon the close of business hours on October 26, 2026," the bank said in a statement to exchanges on Saturday. The bank's board said it will fast-track the process for appointing Jagdishan's successor. "The new CEO will have their task cut out given the ongoing challenges at the bank. They'll have also to retain talent and ensure a seamless transition," said Anand Dama, executive director at Mumbai-based brokerage firm Nuvama. "My sense is that the likelihood of the bank getting an external candidate is higher," he said. SHARES UNDER PRESSURE HDFC Bank, in which foreign investors held nearly a 40% share as of June, has seen its stock price fall 27% since the start of the year with a large part of the losses coming after the former chairman's abrupt departure in March. Investors have also [USN:L4N40B0WF TEXT:"raised concerns"] over the lack of gains from a 2023 merger with its then parent HDFC Ltd. The bank's shares slipped to a more than two-year low on Thursday after a couple of U.S. law firms filed a proposed federal securities class action suit. The bank, in a statement to Reuters, said it "believes the lawsuit is without merit and intends to vigorously defend itself." G Chokkalingam, founder and head of research at market advisory firm Equinomics Research, said the bank's stock could fall 2% to 3% on Monday in a knee-jerk reaction to the news. "However, a bank with such a large and strong balance sheet will not find it difficult to attract good talent," he said, adding that the lender now trades at less than twice its book value, making the stock attractive to long-term investors. HDFC Bank reported a 5% rise in standalone net profit of 190.60 billion Indian rupees ($2.0 billion) for the quarter ended June 30. Gross non-performing loans as a share of total loans are low at 1.17%.

item.title: Niger-Des soldats mutins attaquent l'aéroport de Niamey et le palais présidentiel
item.description: Des soldats mutins au Niger ont attaqué samedi dans la matinée l'aéroport et la présidence à Niamey, la capitale du pays, déclenchant une riposte des forces loyalistes, alors que des tirs nourris et des explosions ont été entendus, tandis que la télévision et la radio d'État ont été brièvement mises hors service.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Des soldats mutins au Niger ont attaqué samedi dans la matinée l'aéroport et la présidence à Niamey, la capitale du pays, déclenchant une riposte des forces loyalistes, alors que des tirs nourris et des explosions ont été entendus, tandis que la télévision et la radio d'État ont été brièvement mises hors service. En fin de matinée, le ministère de la Défense du Niger a déclaré que les forces armées reprenaient progressivement le contrôle des sites ciblés, mais des sources sécuritaires ont indiqué que des mutins étaient toujours présents à l'aéroport et que la situation générale restait floue. La télévision et la radio d'État ont été mis hors service à 8 heures du matin, heure locale (8 heures GMT), avant de reprendre par la suite ses programmes. La télévision d'État a notamment diffusé un message indiquant que des soldats mutins d'une base de Niamey avaient ouvert le feu sur des "sites sensibles" dans la ville. Les forces de sécurité ont réagi rapidement et "maîtrisé les troubles", a-t-elle indiqué. C'est la troisième fois depuis le début de l'année que Niamey - et plus précisément le complexe abritant l'aéroport international et une base aérienne militaire – enregistre d'importants troubles. Un climat d'insécurité demeure au Niger depuis la prise du pouvoir par les militaires à la suite d'un coup d'Etat survenu en 2023 qui a porté le général Abdourahamane Tiani à la tête du pays. Ce dernier s'était engagé à améliorer la sécurité dans ce pays du Sahel, important producteur d'uranium, mais les attaques djihadistes persistent. En début d'année, des groupes affiliés à Al Qaïda et à l'Etat islamique ont ainsi mené des attaques contre l'aéroport civil et la base aérienne militaire attenante. L'assaut de samedi a duré des heures et impliqué des soldats des localités d'Ouallam, de Tera et de Dosso, dans le sud-ouest du pays, ont déclaré à Reuters une source sécuritaire nigérienne, ainsi qu'Yvan Guichaoua, chercheur au Centre international d'études des conflits de Bonn. Les troupes déployées dans cette zone ont subi de lourdes pertes lors des combats contre la branche régionale de l'Etat islamique. "Des affrontements sont en cours au Niger et la situation reste confuse", a prévenu le Quai d'Orsay sur son site internet, rappelant que l'Ambassade de France à Niamey est fermée jusqu'à nouvel ordre et n'est plus en mesure d'assurer l'assistance consulaire. "Il est rappelé qu’il est formellement déconseillé de se rendre au Niger, quel que soit le motif. Les ressortissants français encore présents au Niger sont appelés à faire preuve de la plus grande vigilance. Il est essentiel de limiter ses déplacements, d’éviter impérativement tout rassemblement et de se tenir informés de l’évolution de la situation." UNE "ATTAQUE LÂCHE", DÉNONCE UN RESPONSABLE NIGÉRIEN Une autre source sécuritaire avait dans un premier temps rapporté à Reuters que des "terroristes" avaient attaqué l'aéroport international Diori Hamani et tenté de pénétrer au-delà du périmètre de sécurité entourant le palais présidentiel. Un journaliste de Reuters avait également rapporté avoir entendu des tirs nourris aux abords de la présidence aux premières heures de l'aube. À 9h00 GMT, le palais présidentiel semblait avoir été sécurisé par les troupes loyalistes, mais la zone autour de l'aéroport était toujours contestée, ont indiqué deux sources sécuritaires et un diplomate. Deux sources ont indiqué que des troupes loyalistes avaient été dépêchées pour reprendre le contrôle de l'aéroport, soit par la négociation, soit par la force. Selon des analystes et des sources sécuritaires, la frustration envers le gouvernement monte au sein des unités de première ligne. Bana Wagana Ibrahim, membre du Bureau du Niger au sein du Conseil consultatif et député au Parlement de l'Alliance des Etats du Sahel (AES), a déclaré sur Facebook que la Base 101, une importante installation militaire à Niamey, avait été prise pour cible, ajoutant que les forces de sécurité avait repris le contrôle. "Une autre attaque lâche contre la base 101 et encore une fois nos forces de défense et de sécurité ont assuré(...) Situation sous contrôle", a-t-il écrit. Reuters n'a pas été en mesure de vérifier ces informations de manière indépendante. Un porte-parole du gouvernement nigérien n'a pas répondu dans l'immédiat à une demande de commentaires. LE NIGER, PRODUCTEUR CLÉ D'URANIUM Le Niger, pays d'Afrique de l'Ouest riche en minéraux et possédant d'importantes ressources en uranium, en pétrole et en or, est dirigé par des militaires depuis le coup d'État de juillet 2023 qui a renversé le président Mohamed Bazoum. Comme ses voisins le Mali et le Burkina Faso, le Niger fait face à une insurrection armée de groupes djihadistes liés à Al Qaïda et l'Etat islamique et n'est jusqu'ici pas parvenu à inverser la tendance, malgré les promesses des dirigeants militaires d'améliorer la sécurité. La branche ouest-africaine d'Al Qaïda a revendiqué l'attentat perpétré en juin contre l'aéroport de Niamey, cinq mois après que l'Etat islamique au Sahel a ciblé le même site. Le gouvernement d'Abdourahamane Tiani a décidé de tourner le dos aux partenaires occidentaux traditionnels du Niger et d'approfondir ses liens avec la Russie. Il a également rompu ses liens avec le bloc régional de la CEDEAO pour rejoindre le Mali et le Burkina Faso afin de former un bloc dissident. Ces troubles surviennent alors que les autorités nigériennes renforcent leur contrôle sur le secteur de l'uranium, après avoir saisi des actifs du groupe français Orano. Le Niger est un fournisseur clé de combustible nucléaire pour l'Europe, représentant environ 15% de l'approvisionnement en uranium d'Orano à pleine capacité. La semaine dernière, le gouvernement a réattribué les anciens permis d'exploitation d'uranium d'Orano et de GoviEx à des entreprises soutenues par l'Etat, conformément à un décret.

item.title: Une frappe russe près de Kyiv provoque une explosion et fait 37 morts
item.description: Une frappe aérienne russe sur un entrepôt dans la région de Kyiv, survenue dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, a provoqué une explosion et fait au moins 37 morts, ont indiqué samedi les autorités ukrainiennes.
item.dc:creator: Reuters
item.content:encoded: Une frappe aérienne russe sur un entrepôt dans la région de Kyiv, survenue dans la nuit de vendredi à samedi, a provoqué une explosion et fait au moins 37 morts, ont indiqué samedi les autorités ukrainiennes. Le président ukrainien Volodimir Zelensky a demandé des comptes après cette explosion survenue dans un entrepôt, dont le bilan est l'un des plus lourds de ces derniers mois et qui semble être le deuxième incident de ce type en deux mois. "Ceux qui ont laissé cela se produire doivent répondre de leurs décisions", a-t-il écrit sur le réseau social X, ajoutant que des poursuites pénales avaient déjà été ouvertes pour négligence officielle. "La réglementation est en vigueur : les munitions ne peuvent être stockées à proximité des habitations ou d'autres zones résidentielles. Les conclusions qui s'imposent seront certainement tirées", a-t-il ajouté. Des dizaines de personnes ont été blessées et plus de 370 personnes ont été évacuées de la zone de la frappe dans le village de Myla, a poursuivi le chef de l'Etat ukrainien. Les infrastructures avoisinantes ont subi des "dégâts importants", a-t-il ajouté, notamment des bâtiments résidentiels et un établissement de soins pour personnes âgées. LA RUSSIE INTENSIFIE SON OFFENSIVE DANS LES AIRS La Russie a intensifié son offensive aérienne contre l'Ukraine, utilisant davantage de missiles balistiques et de drones à réaction difficiles à abattre. Neuf autres régions ukrainiennes ont été visées par des frappes nocturnes menées par la Russie, selon Volodimir Zelensky, notant que la capitale est soumise à des attaques "quasi ininterrompues" de drones à grande vitesse. Des sirènes ont retenti toute la matinée, pour le troisième jour consécutif, l'armée de l'air ukrainienne mettant en garde contre de nouvelles vagues de drones approchant de la capitale. Le chef de l'administration de la région de Kyiv, Tymur Tkachenko, a déclaré qu'une jeune fille de 14 ans avait été tuée samedi lors d'une frappe de drones dans le district de Boryspil. A Kyiv, une fillette de deux ans a été tuée par un drone abattu, a dit pour sa part samedi le maire de la ville, Vitali Klitschko. Les frappes survenues jeudi et vendredi à Kyiv et dans ses environs ont endommagé des entrepôts et des habitations. Certains responsables ukrainiens présentent cette offensive russe comme une campagne visant à "paralyser" la ville. La récente explosion fait suite à un incident similaire survenu le mois dernier à Vyshneve, une ville de la région de Kyiv, où 10 personnes avaient été tuées et des centaines de maisons endommagées après qu'une frappe a déclenché des explosions secondaires. "En cette cinquième année de guerre totale, nous n'avons pas le droit de permettre la répétition de tragédies comme celle qui s'est produite à Vyshneve, et celle survenue dans le district de Boutcha", a écrit sur Telegram le Premier ministre Sergii Koretskyi, qui s'est rendu sur le lieu de l'explosion de vendredi. Moscou a par ailleurs annoncé samedi avoir prolongé jusqu'au 30 septembre son interdiction sur les exportations russes de diesel, en vigueur depuis le 8 juillet, confirmant des informations de Reuters. L'interdiction couvre aussi les exportations de carburants maritimes et de dérivés gaziers livrés par les producteurs russes, a ajouté le gouvernement dans un communiqué. L'objectif, selon les sources, est de faire face à des pénuries persistantes de carburants sur le sol russe, où plusieurs raffineries sont toujours hors service après des frappes répétées de drones ukrainiens.

item.description: Aug 29 : Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi became the first rider to crack the one minute and 45 seconds barrier at MotorLand, snatching pole position for the Aragon Grand Prix and ending Marc Marquez's bid for a hat-trick of poles at the circuit on Saturday.The Italian initially set the pace with a time of 1:44.984
item.dc:creator: CNA
item.content:encoded:

Aug 29 : Aprilia's Marco Bezzecchi became the first rider to crack the one minute and 45 seconds barrier at MotorLand, snatching pole position for the Aragon Grand Prix and ending Marc Marquez's bid for a hat-trick of poles at the circuit on Saturday. The Italian initially set the pace with a time of 1:44.984 before going even faster with another lap record of 1:44.962, leaving Ducati's Marquez unable to match the Aprilia rider's scorching pace. Marquez, who has won seven MotoGP races at Aragon, will start alongside Bezzecchi on the front row despite a heart-stopping moment while braking on a flying lap. His brother Alex Marquez, of Gresini Racing, completes the front row. "Well, it was a positive morning overall... Obviously, the qualifying was good fun. I'm happy to be fast and to grab the pole position," Bezzecchi said.

"Now the real job starts... We start in a good place, but Marc and Alex are both super fast in terms of pace with both tyres, so it's going to be a tough fight. But we are enjoying and let's see what we can do." Reigning world champion Marc Marquez accepted that Bezzecchi had the faster bike. "Marco, at the moment, has a better pace than us, so sometimes you cannot do anything. You just try to do your best and it's what we are doing," he said. "I pushed hard on that brake point, maybe too much and I had that moment. I feel that I can keep a constant pace, but Marco basically has a bit faster pace." Trackhouse Racing's Raul Fernandez was fourth-fastest and he will line up on the second row with Aprilia's Jorge Martin and KTM's Pedro Acosta. The third row features VR46 Racing's Fabio Di Giannantonio, Ducati's Francesco Bagnaia and LCR Honda's Johann Zarco, who made a memorable return from a knee injury sustained in a crash at the Catalan Grand Prix in May.
